title: Basic try-except with Specific Exception Handlers
code:
# Demonstrating basic exception catching with distinct feedback
def calculate_ratio(num_str, denom_str):
    try:
        numerator = float(num_str)
        denominator = float(denom_str)
        result = numerator / denominator
        print("Ratio:", result)
    except ValueError:
        print("Error: Both inputs must be numeric values.")
    except ZeroDivisionError:
        print("Error: Cannot divide by zero.")

print("1. Valid calculation:")
calculate_ratio("10", "2")

print("\n2. Non-numeric input:")
calculate_ratio("abc", "2")

print("\n3. Zero denominator:")
calculate_ratio("10", "0")
explanation: Illustrates how multiple specific except blocks intercept different error types (ValueError vs ZeroDivisionError) to provide targeted user feedback.

title: Complete try-except-else-finally Execution Lifecycle
code:
# Tracing when else and finally execute
def process_transaction(raw_amount):
    print("--- Processing:", raw_amount, "---")
    try:
        amount = int(raw_amount)
        balance = 500 / amount
    except ValueError:
        print("EXCEPT: Invalid number provided")
    except ZeroDivisionError:
        print("EXCEPT: Amount cannot be zero")
    else:
        # Runs ONLY when try finishes with NO exceptions
        print("ELSE: Transaction approved. Balance factor:", balance)
    finally:
        # ALWAYS runs, even after exceptions
        print("FINALLY: Audit log recorded")

process_transaction("50")   # Success case: try -> else -> finally
process_transaction("abc")  # Error case: try -> except -> finally
process_transaction("0")    # Zero case: try -> except -> finally
explanation: Demonstrates the complete try-except-else-finally lifecycle, highlighting that else executes only on success, while finally always executes.

title: Robust File Processing with Exception Handling & Cleanup
code:
# Safely parsing lines of CSV records with try-except
file_records = [
    "Arun,85",
    "Priya,92",
    "Rahul,invalid_score",
    "Meena,78"
]

valid_count = 0
invalid_count = 0

for line in file_records:
    parts = line.split(",")
    name = parts[0]
    raw_score = parts[1]
    
    try:
        score = int(raw_score)
    except ValueError:
        print("Invalid record skipped: %s (score '%s' is not numeric)" % (name, raw_score))
        invalid_count += 1
    else:
        print("Valid student logged: %-8s | Score: %d" % (name, score))
        valid_count += 1
    finally:
        pass  # Per-record cleanup if necessary

print("\nSummary: %d valid records, %d invalid records processed." % (valid_count, invalid_count))
explanation: Simulates robust file line processing where corrupt records are safely logged and skipped without halting the overall data pipeline.
